scientific_integrity: The proof tracks the coprime coefficient and the \(2\)- and \(3\)-adic exponents exactly. Periodicity forces every newly created coprime factor to be \(1\), after which a product identity and a complete treatment of the four possible values below \(6\) force every orbit state to have \(3a+2b=6\). Finite computation is used only as regression evidence.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to positive periodic points for \(S=\{2,3\}\). It does not classify periodic behavior for arbitrary finite prime sets. The fixed-point families are prior-covered; the new claim is the exclusion of every nontrivial positive cycle for this two-prime set.
title: No nontrivial positive cycles for the \(\{2,3\}\)-arithmetic subderivative
